questiontext.text: 1) Which pathways meet the Governing Vessel at Dazhui DU-14?

generalfeedback.text: The six Yang Channels meet the Governing Vessel at Dazhui DU-14. Why are the other options incorrect? The six Yin Channels — The regional statement specifies the Yang rather than the Yin Channels. Only the Bladder and Kidney Channels — The meeting is broader than the Bladder–Kidney pair. Only the Liver and Gall Bladder Channels — The meeting is broader than the Liver–Gall Bladder pair.

questiontext.text: 2) Which vessels meet the Bladder Channel at Jingming BL-1?

generalfeedback.text: Yang Qiao and Yin Qiao meet the Bladder Channel at the inner canthus at Jingming BL-1. Why are the other options incorrect? Girdling and Penetrating vessels — Dai and Chong do not form this named BL-1 meeting. Yang Linking and Yin Linking vessels — The Linking vessels are not the pair specified at BL-1. Governing and Conception vessels only — The BL-1 relationship specifically includes the two Motility vessels and Bladder.

questiontext.text: 3) Which group meets at Jianyu LI-15 according to the regional atlas?

generalfeedback.text: Jianyu LI-15 is shared by Large Intestine Primary and Divergent, Small Intestine Luo and Bladder Sinew relationships. Why are the other options incorrect? Heart Primary, Kidney Luo, Liver Sinew and Dai Mai — This combination does not match the listed LI-15 convergence. Stomach Luo, Spleen Primary, Yin Qiao and Chong Mai — These routes are associated with other regions and systems. Lung Sinew, Pericardium Luo, Gall Bladder Luo and Du Luo — This group is not the supplied meeting at Jianyu LI-15.

generalfeedback.text: At GB-30, compare the Bladder crossing relationship with Gall Bladder emergence and deep hip entry. Why are the other options incorrect? Spleen and Kidney both terminate at the outer canthus. — Spleen and Kidney do not terminate at the outer canthus.

generalfeedback.text: The ear gathering region includes Large Intestine, Stomach, Small Intestine, Gall Bladder and Sanjiao relationships. Why are the other options incorrect? Lung, Spleen, Heart, Kidney and Liver — This is a Yin-organ grouping rather than the supplied ear gathering group. questiontext.text: 6) Why is the supraclavicular fossa a high-value comparison area?

generalfeedback.text: The supraclavicular fossa contains routes from several systems, making depth, action and next destination decisive. Why are the other options incorrect? Only one channel reaches it. — Many pathways reach this area. It identifies every route as Lung Primary. — Lung Primary is only one possible relationship. It contains no transition between depth and surface. — The area is important precisely because routes emerge, pass or transition there.

answer.text: Primary, Divergent, Sinew and Extraordinary routes all reach it.

questiontext.text: 7) Which Sanjiao Primary relationship occurs near Shanzhong REN-17?

generalfeedback.text: The Sanjiao Primary Channel disperses in the chest midway between the breasts near Shanzhong REN-17. Why are the other options incorrect? It originates at the medial heel. — Sanjiao Primary begins at the ring finger, not the medial heel. It binds at the medial knee. — Medial-knee binding belongs to lower-limb relationships. It terminates at the great toe. — Sanjiao Primary does not terminate at the great toe.

questiontext.text: 9) What is the best three-part method for studying a convergence hub?

generalfeedback.text: Incoming route, event at the hub and outgoing route distinguish pathways sharing one landmark. Why are the other options incorrect? Memorize only the point name. — A point name alone does not distinguish all converging routes. Choose the channel with the same color. — Color is not pathway evidence. Ignore what happens before and after the hub. — The surrounding route is required to identify the system and direction.

answer.text: Trace the incoming route, name the event at the hub and follow the outgoing route.
